 Concerns over additional selling in hedge fund losses
'AI genius Leopold is on the verge of liquidation again 사진 확대 New York Stock Exchange [Yonhap News] Investors' fears are at their peak in the U.S. stock market. This is due to the sharp drop in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.
 Investors who are surprised by the fall in stock prices are scrambling to throw out stocks and bring down stock prices again. There are also concerns that even large hedge funds could suffer significant losses and increase market shock.
 According to Reuters on the 5th (local time), the Chicago Option Exchange (CBOE) Volatility Index (VIX) soared to 28.36 during the day, the highest in about eight months. VIX is called the "fear index" because it rises as investors' anxiety grows.
 As the stock market fluctuated, the fear index soared sharply as investors trying to prepare for a fall in stock prices were flocking to buy put options (the right to sell assets at a predetermined price).
 Shortly after the midterm elections, Wall Street banks predicted that the stock market would regain stability due to the resolution of political uncertainty, but they seem to be embarrassed as the dumping of AI-related stocks took place within a day.
 On the same day, social media and others observed that Leopold Ashenbrenner's hedge fund Drilling Aware, which triggered the chaos of technology stocks in July, faced another forced liquidation crisis. The mechanical rebalancing (rebalancing of holdings) of exchange-traded funds (ETFs) also increased selling pressure.
 Nomura Securities estimated that leveraged ETFs sold about $47 billion on the same day. Even individual investors are estimated to have sold a net $338 million worth this time.
 However, some say that the stock market is close to the bottom. "Additional forced liquidation may occur, but it is likely that the "surrender sale" of dumping stocks has entered its final stage," said Alan Huang, vice president of Mega Financial Holdings.
